cases.description: An empty file has no signature.
The signature must be 'skyb'.
The file ends in the middle of the signature.
The file ends after the signature.
Versioning starts at version 1.
The highest supported version is version 2.
A version 1 file may consist of the header only.
Version 2 files must have a features byte.
The file ends in the middle of the CRC32 checksum.
Version 2 file without a checksum.
Version 2 file with a correct CRC32 checksum.
The checksum does not match the contents of the file.
Reserved bits of the features byte are ignored.
Reserved bits of the features byte are ignored when a checksum is also present.
The file ends after the type byte of the first block.
The file ends in the middle of the length field of the first block.
The file is shorter than the length declared in the header of a block.
Blocks before a truncated block can still be loaded.
Block type 0x00 ends the list of blocks; blocks after it are ignored.
Blocks with unknown types are skipped.
When a block type appears multiple times, the first block is used.
Blocks may appear in any order.
Linear segment along all three axes, scale 10.
Only the X coordinate changes; Y and Z are constant and have no control points.
Cubic Bezier segment along the X axis with control points 0, 0, 100, 100.
Seventh-degree Bezier segment along the X axis with evenly spaced control points.
Consecutive segments start where the previous segment ended.
A zero-duration segment is an instantaneous jump; within the segment the position is the midpoint of the jump.
A scale factor of zero means that the trajectory is empty.
Legacy embedded yaw track: the yaw is ignored but its control points are skipped.
Legacy embedded yaw track with a cubic Bezier yaw axis followed by another segment.
The trajectory block is shorter than its header.
The trajectory block has no header.
The trajectory block ends in the middle of a segment header.
The trajectory block ends in the middle of a control point.
The trajectory block ends before the legacy yaw control points declared by the segment.
An empty light program is black and ends immediately.
Set a color, then fade to another one; intermediate components are truncated.
Grayscale, white and black set and fade opcodes.
Durations are varints and may span multiple bytes.
SLEEP waits without changing the color; NOP does nothing.
WAIT_UNTIL waits until the given frame since the start; a deadline in the past is a no-op.
Reaching the end of the block behaves like END.
Arguments truncated by the end of the block read as zeros.
An unknown opcode stops the program and the current color is held.
A fade with zero duration sets the target color immediately, and the next fade starts from it.
A loop with three iterations; commands due at the same instant are all executed at that instant.
A loop with a single iteration runs once.
A loop with an iteration count of zero repeats forever.
Two nested loops with two iterations each.
The reference implementation supports four levels of nested loops.
Exceeding the maximum nesting depth stops the program and the current color is held.
A LOOP_END without a matching LOOP_BEGIN is a no-op.
An infinite loop whose iteration takes no time stops the program.
An infinite loop whose later iterations take no time (because the deadline of WAIT_UNTIL is in the past) stops the program.
Finite loops whose iterations take no time are allowed.
Yaw offset followed by two yaw deltas with linear interpolation.
The auto flag is exposed as-is; negative offsets and deltas are allowed.
Parsers use the yaw offset as-is, without taking it modulo 3600.
Reserved bits of the flags byte are ignored.
A zero-duration delta is an instantaneous change; within the delta the yaw is the midpoint of the change.
The yaw control block has no header.
The yaw control block ends in the middle of the yaw offset.
The yaw control block ends in the middle of a delta.
Pyro trigger and light control events; events with equal timestamps are allowed.
Unknown event types and subtypes are kept as opaque events; trailing bytes are ignored.
An empty event list block contains no events.
Event lists that are not sorted by timestamp are rejected.
RTH plan with two points and two entries; point coordinates are scaled but acceleration and speed are not.
The MSB of the scale byte is reserved and ignored.
An RTH plan without points and without an entry table has no entries.
The RTH plan block is shorter than its header.
The RTH plan block ends in the middle of the point array.
The RTH plan block ends in the middle of the number of entries.
The RTH plan block contains fewer entries than declared.
The RTH plan block ends in the middle of the neck length of an entry.
The RTH plan block ends in the middle of a varuint in an entry.
Varints may be five bytes long; the time of the only entry is UINT32_MAX seconds.
A varint may use more bytes than necessary as long as it is at most five bytes long.
An entry with a varint that does not fit into 32 bits does not make the RTH plan invalid.
An entry whose activation timestamp does not fit into 32 bits does not make the RTH plan invalid.
An entry with a duration longer than 2^24 seconds does not make the RTH plan invalid.
An entry that refers to a point that does not exist does not make the RTH plan invalid.
Coordinates, color palette and matrix size.
Missing tags take their default values.
Entries with unknown tags are skipped.
When a tag appears multiple times, the last occurrence wins.
4095 is the largest valid coordinate.
0 is the smallest valid coordinate.
Coordinates must be smaller than 4096.
Coordinates must not be negative.
Matrix sizes must be smaller than 4096.
The value of the coordinates entry must be four bytes long.
The length of the color palette must be a multiple of three.
An entry with an empty value may end exactly at the end of the block.
The value of an entry extends beyond the end of the block.
Show ID and drone index.
Missing tags take their default values.
Entries with unknown tags are skipped.
When a tag appears multiple times, the last occurrence wins.
The show ID must be four bytes long.
The drone index must be two bytes long.
